subject: Food Science
title: E. coli O157:H7
description: A quick, practical guide to E. coli O157:H7.

hook.text: In 1993, contaminated Jack in the Box burgers sickened 732 people and killed 4 children. E. coli O157:H7 became infamous.

buildup.text: E. coli O157:H7 produces Shiga toxin that destroys kidney cells—causing bloody diarrhea and sometimes kidney failure.

discovery.text: Just 10 cells can cause infection. It lives in cattle intestines and reaches beef during slaughter.

twist.text: Ground beef is riskier than steaks because grinding disperses surface bacteria throughout the meat.

climax.text: That's why steaks can be served rare—bacteria stay on the surface. Burgers must reach 71°C all the way through.

punchline.text: Rare steak is safe. Rare burger isn't. Grinding spreads the danger inside.

quiz.question: Why is ground beef riskier than steak for E. coli?
options: Grinding disperses surface bacteria throughout the meat
